newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Notionnel vol up, deficit worries loom.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Notionnel vol up, deficit worries loom.

text.p: Implied volatility of front month notionnel options traded on MATIF rose on Tuesday, amid concerns the new Socialist government will not tackle the budget deficit, traders said on Tuesday.

French Finance minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn has said his country is determined to stick to the Maastricht Treaty, and launch the new currency on time. The Treaty calls for countries to cut the deficit/GDP ratio to, or towards, three percent, leaving debate about the interpretation.

"Everyone is waiting for July 21, when the government is expected to announced what it will do to the budget deficit," said an options broker at a French house in Paris. "Volatility could rise towards that."

August options volatility on the September notionnel future rose to 4.24 percent, compared with around 4.0 percent at the prior close. September was up to 4.40 percent, compared with 4.3 percent, but December was little changed to slightly weaker at 5.90 pecent.
September notionnel futures were down four basis points at 130.48, after earlier setting a new contract high of 130.66, while December was down two basis points at 99.14.

Strauss-Kahn repeated earlier on Thursday that an audit of public finances due on July 21 would reveal that France's public deficit would be "higher" than the 3.0 percent forecast in the 1997 finance act, mainly because of a shortfall in revenues.
"There's some concern the new government will show its true colours then," said a trader at a French bank.
"They have to tacke the fiscal side, and I don't think they're prepared to do that."
Traders said volatility had reached a sturdy level of support, as investors who had bought volatility were not prepared to sell at the current low levels.

In the August options, put buying was popular at the 130.00 strike where more than 1,300 lots had traded by 0945 GMT. In September, put spreads took the lion's share of trade, and the 127.00 and 129.00 strikes.
Pibor options volatility rose slightly, with August at 12.5 percent compared with 12.4 percent yesterday, and September up to 13.5 percent compared with 13.0 percent.
